audits.text:
## dc3b5c670093

**A-DC3B-1 — Reproduced teaching defect: clipped query after complete-block demonstrations.** The unchanged generator produces lessons in which a simple canonical-fitting rival explains every demonstration but predicts a different query answer. The rival doubles the 2×2 template rightward and stops before a block would cross the right border. The intended rule clips that block to the visible canvas.

The production CLI generated the witness with **seed 2, difficulty `hard`, no overrides, sample indices `[0,1,2,3]`, three demonstrations and one query, in its original order**. No query rotation or hand-built lesson was used.

| Role | Sample index | Grid | Template top row | Rival agrees with actual Racket? |
|---|---:|---|---:|---|
| Demonstration 1 | 0 | 16×30 | 7 | Yes |
| Demonstration 2 | 1 | 16×30 | 7 | Yes |
| Demonstration 3 | 2 | 10×14 | 4 | Yes |
| Query | 3 | 16×18 | 9 | No: 56 cells differ |

On the query, Racket paints the visible part of the scale-8 block at zero-based rows **2–15**, columns **14–17**. The rival leaves those 56 cells zero; for example, `(2,14)` is **5** under Racket and **0** under the rival. Every witness input passes the target's `self_check`, belongs to its documented domain, and was produced by the unchanged generator. All eight stored canonical pair positions (four unique pairs) also fit this rival, confirmed against both saved canonical labels and the supported Racket `apply` route.

**Measured scope.** In **32 hard production lessons, seeds 0–31, samples 0–3 per seed**, the complete-width rival fit all demonstrations and disagreed on the query in **4/32 lessons**, seeds **2, 3, 22, 23**. There were **128/128 unique generated inputs**, **128/128 validator passes**, no generation rejections, and **128/128** agreement between the generated Racket labels and the audit's independent clipped-staircase rendering. A second rival that stops at any canvas border had the same four ambiguous lessons; a third that centers enlargements on the canvas had **3/32**, seeds **2, 3, 23**. All three fit **8/8** stored canonical pair positions. The target declares neither `CANONICAL_SHORTCUTS` nor `LESSON_COMPETITORS`; these are explicitly auditor-supplied probes. This is a teaching defect, with no incorrect Racket labels reproduced.

**Source identity.** Generator version `3.0.0`, SHA-256 `3e82bde5d4a3421d9d476e992f8a48223de34b1ec18645e1363609af2ebb3bd2`; catalog and executed rule identifier `dc5d69bcdd26`; exact canonical program text SHA-256 `a8cf63616699adca2649a53b95ac872ad8c6a2c9fe8039a4d26d9edb547eebb9`; executed callable text SHA-256 `0f86ff85ec91c41cd978a7f98e07ae991fda19e1ec46677af315a599564d66cd`. The public apply receipt reports `rule_hash_matches_catalog=true` and no errors on its 12 input positions (eight canonical plus four witness inputs).

**Evidence.** `checks/audit/dc3b5c670093/witness.json` contains the exact generated inputs, axes, validator/domain status, sample indices, actual Racket outputs, rival outputs, differing cells, hashes and apply command. `racket.json` is the unedited supported apply receipt; `input.json` retains its input order. `episodes.jsonl` retains all 32 production lessons; `summary.json` records denominators and every ambiguous seed; `audit_probe.py` replays the rivals. `commands.json` contains exact argument arrays, packet-root and payload working directories, source hash, evidence paths and exit statuses. Generate, prepare, apply and finalize all exited **0**.

**Suggested repair, not applied in this audit.** Declare the clipping and centering competitors and require a distinguishing demonstration whenever the query needs those behaviors. Keep generalized geometry, while making each lesson teach the generalization it tests. The audit made no generator or reference-rule changes.

**Limits.** This focused check covered only 32 hard lessons with the production three-demonstration/one-query order and the three stated rivals. It did not run the full battery, easy/medium lesson sampling, override enumeration, query rotations or a universal identifiability proof. The 4/32 figure describes this exact retained finite sample, not an estimated corpus-wide failure rate.
